# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 33 (Bu-Vb Sk33)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Sk33
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 33
**Title (English, from literature):** Not eating in order

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 33 is the thirty-third training rule (*sekhiya*) in the Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka, titled *Sapadāna* ("Not eating in order"). The training rule governs monastic meal etiquette, requiring monks to eat almsfood in proper sequence without disrupting the order (*sapadānaṃ*), a term explained in Vinaya and commentarial contexts as moving successively and without break [Vinaya Pitaka vol 4 - Mahavagga_]. A modern English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

Theravāda parallels within the Pali Canon include the corresponding rule in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-sk33*), the Bhikkhu Parivāra, the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga (*pli-tv-bi-vb-sk33*), the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha, and the Bhikkhunī Parivāra. Extensive cross-tradition parallels are attested in the Vinayas of other early Buddhist schools preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, and Dharmaguptaka traditions, as well as the *Upāliparipṛcchā*. In automated text-reuse analysis, DharmaNexus identifies 93 matching passages across 38 Pali texts, displaying heavy formulaic overlap with neighboring Sekhiya rules on eating decorum, most notably Sekhiya 31 (§0.1–1.17), Sekhiya 35 (§0.1–1.10), Sekhiya 46 (§1.1–1.9), and Sekhiya 32 (§1.2–1.7) [DharmaNexus].
